Any finite relational candidate must supply a limit construction whose pure-state space is a compact homogeneous space under a connected group, and tomographic locality, before continuous-reversibility reconstructions of quantum theory apply. The limit is not canonical: the cyclic groups Z_n have a direct-limit closure U(1), which is connected, and an inverse limit, the profinite integers, which is totally disconnected. Paper G7 restricts the form of the limit: a finite subset of the Bloch sphere that is homogeneous leaves a cap of angular radius arccos(59/60) = 10.475 degrees uncovered, 14.835 degrees for orbits of rotation groups (G7-01-07), and by the theorems of Turing and Gelander no quantum pure-state space is a Gromov-Hausdorff limit of finite homogeneous metric spaces (G7-01-09). Finite stages therefore cannot have a transitive symmetry group; inhomogeneous approximants, finite generating data with unbounded words, and cyclic-group-valued phases remain. Edition Z2: for the second and third forms paper G8 gives a construction conditional on stated assumptions (events of unbounded walk length on a finite gain graph give, under a growth condition, a dense inhomogeneous subset of a complex or real projective space; G8-01-05); Directors A and B record inhomogeneous nets of an imported geometry. A connected group acting on the limit, and tomographic locality as a principle, are not obtained.

statement: A reason for requiring that pure states form a symplectic manifold that does not presuppose Hamiltonian dynamics, and its relation to observability of energy and to tomographic locality as alternative postulates selecting complex amplitudes. Edition Z2: the symplectic form, the complex holonomy commutant, a dynamical correspondence (Alfsen-Shultz) and observability of energy are forms of one requirement, and equality of the numbers of generators and observables is necessary for it (G7-01-12). A warrant for the requirement is not identified. Edition Z3: a real reversible step has a complex structure of its own, unique under positivity of the generator and reversed with the step (G9-01-05); Stueckelberg (1960) and Moretti-Oppio (2017, for Poincare symmetry) are the corresponding results in the literature. In the model of G9 the record projections do not commute with it and the commutant of step and records is real (G9-01-06). This route gives a warrant only if the observables are those generated by the dynamics, which is the requirement in another form. On signed Cayley rectagraphs a central complex structure exists exactly for k = 3 mod 4 direction classes, with k supplied (G9-01-12). A warrant is not identified.

For any of the three remaining forms of a finite-to-continuum limit (inhomogeneous approximants, finite generating data, cyclic-group-valued phases): a construction from a finite relational structure that yields a transition-probability geometry of the comparison class, together with a rule for composing systems. Edition Z2: the transport construction of the Bargmann phase itself is given (G7-01-10). Paper G8 gives a conditional construction for the second and third forms with a composition rule (G8-01-05, G8-01-06); open are a reason for the second order of the rule, for the record role of end vertices and for the group and representation, the growth condition, and any construction for the first form that does not import the geometry. Edition Z3: the growth condition is settled (G8-01-10): it holds exactly when the closed walks of even length realize every group element, and the type of the limit space follows the group they realize. A representation-free form of the rule is the coincidence count on the covering graph (G8-01-09). Open are a reason for the second order (an additive weighting of returning walks exists: G8-01-01), for the record role of end vertices, for the group and representation, and any construction for the first form that does not import the geometry. Edition Z4: the second order is derived conditionally (G10-01-03, G10-01-04): if events are sets of histories, a rule that adds over end vertices a function of the modulus of the summed gains is consistent only for the square on the signed line, and only for the second power on any norm-preserving gain digraph with a merging pair of walks. The additive weighting of returning walks is excluded under the same assumption (G10-01-02). With trivial gains the count is consistent on the same carrier. Open are a reason for the event structure, for the record role of end vertices and the record-sum form, for the carrier, for the group and representation, and any construction for the first form that does not import the geometry. Edition Z5: the square is forced on every finite connected signed gain digraph that is norm-preserving of degree two, whatever its base digraph (G10-01-07); for gains of order four the same is observed on ten carriers and not proved. Edition Z6: for gains in the q-th roots of unity the consistent rules of the record-sum form are exactly the combinations of the squared moduli in the conjugate characters (G10-01-09), under a growth hypothesis on one block that holds on the two-vertex carrier with step matrix [[1, zeta], [1, -zeta]]. The order of the rule is forced; the representation is not.

statement: Orientation. The transition probabilities leave one conjugation per system undetermined (G7-01-11); conjugating a whole model changes no outcome probability (Director B, B2); a composite fixes the relative orientations of its parts, which form a balanced signing (G7-01-15). What fixes the relative orientations in a structure specified without quantum data, and which equivalence relation a candidate is required to respect, are not identified. Edition Z3: where a reversible real step defines a complex structure, its orientation is the direction of the step (G9-01-05); on a signed cube it is the orientation of the three direction classes (G9-01-12). Neither is a structure that the records of the model respect, and neither fixes relative orientations of several systems.

Ordering of values. Algebraic generating data determine transition probabilities only up to field automorphisms (G7-01-13); for cyclic phases the pair measure is independent of the faithful character only for orders 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (G8-01-08). A principle that supplies the ordering of the values of a probability, or that confines the data to the rational, Gaussian or Eisenstein fields, is not given. A directed three-cycle yields the Eisenstein field and equally a classical simplex (Director A, A2). Edition Z3: in the constructed trial GH-2 a weak force requires a linear gain in a cyclic group of large order, for which the measure depends on the character; with orders 2, 3, 4, 6 the field is strong, and a staircase of order-4 gains does not follow the ray of its mean field (G9 Section 6.2; OP-28). Edition Z6: consistency on history events does not supply the ordering. The consistent rules for gains of order q form a space of dimension phi(q)/2 spanned by the squared moduli of the conjugate characters, so the rule is unique exactly for the orders 2, 4, 6 (G10-01-09); for other orders every embedding, and every combination with unequal weights, is consistent. Director G (Codex participant, 13 November 2026, review thread of the program) reports an instance on five sheets with three-step values (3 + sqrt 5)/16 and (3 - sqrt 5)/16 under two embeddings, and is examining which measurement assumptions select the ordinary embedding; not inspected by Director Z. Edition Z7: multiplicativity on products of carriers removes the combinations: a consistent multiplicative rule is the squared modulus in one conjugate character (G10-01-10). Director G (pull request 2, commit b626c0d) obtained first, from a marginal test with one balanced coin, invariance under zeta and factorization of product tables on Q(zeta, sqrt 2), that the weight is lambda(a conj a) for a field embedding lambda of the real subfield; Director Z read that proof and confirmed its linear-algebra core by an exact computation (invariant forms of dimension phi(M) for M = 3, 5, 7, 9, spanned by the embeddings). What remains is the Galois group acting on one character. Director G lists three controls that would break it (a regular real plane, an order on the real algebraic amplitudes, a calibrated preparation with a prescribed algebraic entry) and shows that a localized sheet with native operations cannot; none is derived from the carrier.

Composition. Single-system data are shared by the minimal composite, the quantum composite and the interpolated family K_t (G7-01-14; Directors B and G); the uniform four-system extension of K_t fails closure under parallel preparation by t(1-t)/4 (Director G); closure under local unitaries and a controlled-not forces the quantum composite once a complex representation is given (Director G; rerun, not reproved). The product of gain graphs gives the full tensor product with a common step count (G8-01-06). A principle selecting the composite, multipartite closure, and the origin of entangling operations are not derived. Edition Z3: the interpolated family K_t is not closed under selective local filters (Directors A, B); no four-party weight repairs it (Director A); a matching-generated hierarchy is closed under parallel preparation, discarding and unconditioned one-site channels and excludes GHZ (Director A); one pure entangled seed with local unitaries and local filters gives all two-qubit states (Directors A, B). All within the imported quantum formalism; recomputed. The product of gain graphs gives the tensor product at each length and can reach fewer end-vertex pairs over all lengths (Director G; G8 Section 6). Which selective operations are available is a further obligation.

Dynamics, clock and classical limit. Static transition-probability geometry selects no generator and no clock (Director A). In the constructed trial GH-1 walk length is not a unitary evolution and only the counting measure of recorded walks is obtained on the classical side (paper G8, Section 9). No reversible dynamics, calibrated time or classical Hamiltonian mechanics has been obtained from any structure of the program. Edition Z3: requiring consistency of the pair measure under continuation makes the step unitary up to a factor (G9-01-01); this admits permutations without transport, involutions on undirected gain graphs, and for out-degree two the arc digraph of a 2-in 2-out digraph with a sign -1 (G9-01-02 to G9-01-04). For the signed arc digraph of a ring the position over steps has the distribution of a group velocity (quoted), a linear gain translates the quasi-momentum exactly (G9-01-09) and packets follow the rays of w(k) + Phi x over one period in instances. Supplied: the requirement, the ring, the step count, the gain order for a weak force. Not obtained: a clock with a unit, a generator other than a choice of logarithm, an error bound for the position equation, interaction, composition, more than one dimension, and classical Hamiltonian mechanics beyond the rays of a given dispersion function. Edition Z4: the continuation requirement is equivalent to taking events to be sets of histories (G10-01-01). An exact force of size 2 pi / n needs gains of order at least n (G10-01-05); the remainder of the ray position after the connection offset falls about as the first power of the field for the packet-averaged ray in computed instances and does not fall for the ray through the central quasi-momentum (G10 Section 7). No bound, clock, composition or interaction. Edition Z7: Director G (pull request 2) gives, for a packet near the band edge k = -pi/2 of the signed line walk under a linear gain, a bound on the full spinor against a constant-force Schroedinger envelope, and weak convergence of the scaled lattice position law to a Newtonian trajectory for a shrinking packet. Director Z read the proof and checked the bound by a real-space walk on a ring (three runs; see the cross-review). Conditional on the band preparation, the squared-amplitude readout, the scaling of lattice variables and gains whose order grows as the field decreases; no clock.

Relation between walk lengths and order of the rule. Consistency of the pair measure under continuation is a requirement that a generic gain graph violates (Directors A, B; G9-01-01); a reason for it, or an alternative relation between the measures at different lengths, is not given. An additive weighting of returning walks by a class function of their holonomy is switching invariant (G8-01-01); a reason for excluding it, if the second-order rule is intended, is not given. Edition Z4: a conditional reason is given. A family of measures is one function on sets of histories exactly when it is consistent under continuation (G10-01-01), and then an additive invariant rule is a multiple of the count (G10-01-02): the first-order weighting of returning walks is not a function of sets of histories. That events are sets of histories is an assumption about the event structure and is not derived.

statement: Force and gain order. Decide whether gains of bounded order (in particular the orders 2, 3, 4, 6 for which the pair measure is independent of the character) can produce the rays of a weak force in a controlled limit, by some encoding other than the staircase tried in G9 Section 6.2, or prove that they cannot. Related: the long-time behaviour under a linear gain depends on the arithmetic of the field (Cedzich et al. 2013). Edition Z4: narrowed. An exact translation of the quasi-momentum needs the linear gain, hence gains of order at least 2 pi / Phi (G10-01-05). For gains of order q >= 3 wound through blocks no quasi-energy lies in the local spectrum of every block, except four band edges for q = 4 (G10-01-06). Instances: staircases of order 3, 4, 6 hold a walk within about one block for block lengths 16 and 64 up to 2048 steps, leak for block length 4 and spread ballistically for block length 1 (Cedzich et al.); an order-4 staircase reaches 0.69, 0.54, 0.16 of the mean-field displacement at block lengths 16, 64, 256. Open: a theorem on the dynamics; arrangements other than staircases (one quasi-periodic rounding was run and stayed within seven sites).
